title: A principal parameter has bounded obstruction near its zero fibre
statement: Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field and $A$ a finite-type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $\pi\in A$ be a non-zero-divisor, meaning multiplication by $\pi$ on $A$ is injective, and suppose every local ring of $A[1/\pi]$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Give $A$ the $k[t]$-algebra structure $t\mapsto\pi$. There exist $q(t)\in k[t]$ with $q(0)\ne0$ and an integer $r\geq1$ such that $\pi^r\in H_{A[1/q(\pi)]/k[t]}$ [def-per-gabber-ramero-obstruction-ideal]. Localization means inverting the powers of the displayed element. The $k[t]$-algebra $A[1/q(\pi)]$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. In particular $D(q(\pi))$ contains all of $V(\pi)$, and passing to it changes none of $A/(\pi^j)$ for $j\geq1$.

proof.text: Put $R=k[t]$ and give $A$ its stated $R$-structure. The same finite set of $k$-algebra generators generates $A$ over $R$. The ring $R$ is Noetherian by [lem-sc-p1-polynomial-noetherian], and $A$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], applied over the field $k$ (its only ideals are $0,k$). Thus $A$ is finitely presented over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]. Every principal localization $A[1/a]$ is finite type over both $k$ and $R$: adjoin the same generators and one generator $z$ with relation $az=1$. The two cited finite-type results therefore give its Noetherianity and finite presentation over $R$ as well.

proof.text: Let $K=k(t)$ and $C=A\otimes_R K$. The maps $a\otimes f/g\mapsto f(\pi)a/g(\pi)$ and $a/g(\pi)\mapsto a\otimes1/g$ identify $C$ with the localization of $A$ at all nonzero polynomials in $\pi$. These formulas are inverse because $g(\pi)\otimes1=1\otimes g(t)$. Since $t$ is among the inverted polynomials, this is also a localization of $A[1/\pi]$. That ring is Noetherian by Step 1 and regular by hypothesis, so [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-regular-ring] makes $C$ regular. It is finite type over $K$, generated by the images of the chosen generators of $A$.

source.place: Tags 00OD (definition-regular-ring), 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization), 00FN; the localization observation in the proof of Tag 0381 (lemma-geometrically-regular)

proof.text: The field $K$ has characteristic zero and is perfect: for an irreducible nonconstant polynomial $p\in K[x]$, its derivative is nonzero and has smaller degree, hence $\gcd(p,p')=1$ and $p$ has no repeated root in any extension. Therefore [lem-trf-regular-perfect-field-smooth], applied to the regular affine $K$-scheme $\operatorname{Spec}C$ of finite type from Step 3, says that its structure morphism is smooth. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], the algebra $C$ is smooth over $K$. These statements also cover $C=0$, whose spectrum is empty; no dominance or nonempty generic fibre has been assumed.

proof.text:
Index all nonzero $g\in R$ by divisibility. This is a small filtered category in the universe of the rings. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-colimit-principal-localizations], $K=\varinjlim_{g
e0}R_g$. In [lem-sbc-smooth-pushout-filtered-colimit-stage] take its fixed map to be $R	o A$, its diagram to be $R_g$, and its pushouts to be $A_g=A\otimes_R R_g$ and $C=A\otimes_R K$. They are pushouts because an $R$-algebra map out of $A_g$ is exactly a map out of $A$ making $g(\pi)$ a unit. The fixed map is finitely presented by Step 1 and the limiting map is smooth by Step 4. The cited node yields a nonzero polynomial $g$ for which $R_g	o A_g$ is smooth. Write $g=t^e h$ with $h(0)
e0$, put $q=q_0h$, and set $B=A[1/q(\pi)]$. Then $q(0)
e0$.

The identity $R\to R$ is smooth by its presentation with zero variables and zero relations in [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-principal-localization], $R\to R_g$ is smooth. Composition [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] now makes $A_g$ smooth over $R$. Its further localization at $q(\pi)\pi$ is $B[1/\pi]$: inverting $q\pi$ already inverts $g=t^e h$, and conversely the two displayed localizations invert the same elements. Principal localization therefore makes $B[1/\pi]$ smooth over $R$. To check flatness of $B$, suppose $f(\pi)(a/q(\pi)^n)=0$ with $f\ne0$. Then $q(\pi)^N f(\pi)a=0$ for some $N$, so $a\in T$, because $q^Nf\ne0$ in $k[t]$. Step 2 gives $q_0(\pi)a=0$, and $q_0(\pi)$ is a unit in $B$ since $q=q_0h$. Thus $a/q(\pi)^n=0$. Hence $B$ is torsion free over the PID $k[t]$ (division with remainder makes every ideal principal), so it is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat]. Its finite presentation over $R$ was proved in Step 1.

Apply [lem-per-gabber-ramero-ideal-calculus] to the Noetherian base $R$ and finitely presented $R$-algebra $B$. Write $H=H_{B/R}$. Its vanishing set is the nonsmooth locus of $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. Step 6 makes the ring map $R\to B[1/\pi]$ smooth, so by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] the open subscheme $D(\pi)=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/\pi]$ of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is smooth over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ in the scheme sense used by the cited calculus. Thus every point outside $V(\pi)$ lies in a smooth open, so every prime containing $H$ contains $\pi$. The equality $\sqrt H=\bigcap_{\mathfrak p\supset H}\mathfrak p$ in [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] gives $\pi\in\sqrt H$. By the displayed power definition of that radical, some integer $r\ge1$ satisfies $\pi^r\in H$, which is the required bound. This argument remains valid when $B=0$.

source.place: §3.2.2 and §3.2.5 (finite conductor); Stacks Algebra Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), radical as intersection of primes

proof.text: Finally write $q(t)=c+t v(t)$ with $c=q(0)\in k^\times$. At every prime containing $\pi$, $q(\pi)$ has image $c$, so $D(q(\pi))$ contains $V(\pi)$. In $A/(\pi^j)$ an inverse of $q(\pi)$ is $c^{-1}\sum_{i=0}^{j-1}(-\pi v(\pi)/c)^i$: multiplying gives $1-(-\pi v(\pi)/c)^j=1$. The fraction map $a/q(\pi)^n\mapsto \bar a\,q(\bar\pi)^{-n}$ therefore defines an inverse to $A/(\pi^j)\to B/(\pi^jB)$. This proves the assertion for every $j\ge1$, including empty zero fibres and the zero ring.
